class_name MatterLedger
extends RefCounted
## The meter of the law of matter (task 66, M0; proposal: .orchestra/tasks/63/matter/spec.md A4): matter never appears or
## vanishes, only a DECLARED flow changes the total of a material. This class does not move anything and rewrites no
## system: it counts (census) what the existing books report and holds the list of declared exceptions.
##
## Unit = kilograms per material id (mass is what a conversion keeps; volume follows from the card's rho).
##
## - Providers: a holder registers itself by NAME with a Callable that returns {material id: kg}. census() sums them:
##   {mat: {total: kg, where: {provider name: kg}}}. Moving, carrying, splitting, building, breaking = the matter goes
##   from one provider to another, the sum stays. No event is needed for that.
## - Events (declared flows, each with material, kg, reason, tick):
##     declare_source(mat, kg, reason)               matter from nothing (map stock, start kit, test range, flora)
##     declare_sink(mat, kg, reason)                 matter into nothing (eaten, removed on the range)
##     declare_transform(from, kg, to, to_kg, reason, loss_name, loss_kg)
##                                                   one material becomes another (rot, grit, smelt). MASS is kept:
##                                                   from_kg == to_kg + loss_kg; a loss must be NAMED (air, vapour, ...)
## - check(prev_census, new_census, events) -> {ok, rows, event_errors, text}: per material the residual
##   (new - prev) - declared change, in kg, against a tolerance; `text` is a readable report.
## - Rules (optional): allow_transform(reason, from families, to families) rejects a transform of the wrong class

## order, so the same events and the same books give the same numbers, byte for byte, on every peer and on every run.

## Rules for the labels of spec A5 (ROT, LITTER, GRIT, PULVERISE, SMELT, BURN). A family is a string the caller gives to
## its materials with set_family (e.g. "wood", "stone", "glass", "soil", "gravel", "ore", "metal", "ash"); a material id
## listed here directly matches too.
static func default_rules() -> Dictionary:
	return {
		"ROT": {from = ["wood"], to = ["humus"]},
		"LITTER": {from = ["foliage"], to = ["humus"]},
		"GRIT": {from = ["stone", "metal"], to = ["gravel", "sand", "dust"]},
		"PULVERISE": {from = ["stone", "glass"], to = ["gravel", "sand", "dust"]},
		"SMELT": {from = ["ore"], to = ["metal"]},
		"BURN": {from = ["wood"], to = ["ash", "charcoal"]},
	}


func use_default_rules() -> void:
	var r := default_rules()
	for reason: String in r:
		allow_transform(reason, r[reason].from, r[reason].to)


func set_family(mat: String, family: String) -> void:
	_family[mat] = family


func set_tolerance(mat: String, kg: float) -> void:
	_tol[mat] = kg


func tolerance_of(mat: String) -> float:
	return float(_tol.get(mat, tolerance_kg))
